summary: Initial scoping call for a 4-6 week POC to evaluate Redwood inference modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) for Oakridge Health's clinical summarization and coding pipeline. Primary success criteria: latency p95 under 450ms for short clinical prompts, throughput to handle 200 concurrent visits during peak, and strict data residency + encrypted-at-rest requirements. Security requirements push deployment toward Dedicated or Private; however cost and speed favor Hosted for an initial functional validation. Team agreed on benchmarks and data artifacts to run a side-by-side test, and next step is SOW + benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Sofia from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we got Ethan our solutions eng and Maya from cs on the line. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Lisa Caldwell: hi Sofia, thanks, lisa here — Head of ML at Oakridge. we've got Amir, jasmine, ryan and nina on. we'll be tight on time so quick agenda: POC scope, success criteria, infra constraints.
[00:19] Ethan Park: great, i'll be driving the technical part. quick confirm — the workloads are clinical summarization + diagnosis coding, mostly short prompts (~150-400 tokens) and some longer chats up to 2k tokens for discharge notes, is that right?
[00:31] Lisa Caldwell: yes that's correct. most queries are short, but the long ones are important for batch jobs overnight. our peak concurrency — we estimate about 200 concurrent sessions across services during morning hours, avg qps per model around 60-80, peak bursts higher.
[00:45] Dr. Amir Patel: also important: PHI data, we need encryption at rest, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs and SOC2 evidence. and we have data residency rules — some data needs to stay in our VPC region.
[00:58] Sofia Martinez: thanks Amir, that's super helpful. wanted to frame the POC: typical 4-6 week POC; goal is to validate correctness, latency/throughput, and integration path. we usually run parallel benchmarks across hosted vs dedicated vs private for like 1-2 days each to show tradeoffs.
[01:14] Jasmine Lee: quick question — with hosted, can you do bring-your-own-key? or do you offer customer KMS?
[01:19] Ethan Park: hosting today supports tenant-level encryption but for customer-managed keys and full audit we generally recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be configured for encrypted transit and at-rest with redwood-managed keys; if BYOK is a blocker then Dedicated/Private are the options. apologies if i mumbled, some transcripts..
[01:32] Nina Gomez: on success criteria — we have product goals: p95 latency < 450ms for short prompts, p50 < 120ms, and end-to-end 95th for long documents under 3s for our batch workflows. cost target is under X per 1k requests but that's negotiable.
[01:47] Ethan Park: ok good. we should capture current baseline — what are you seeing from your in-house?
[01:51] Ryan Cho: baseline is noisy — our internal CPUs give like 1.2s p95 on short prompts, gpu infra is dialed for nightly batches but expensive. cloud LLMs we've tested have good latency but data residency and PHI handling is the blocker.
[02:03] Sofia Martinez: understood. so decision criteria we usually see: 1) security/compliance must-haves (SOC2, BYOK, VPC), 2) latency/throughput targets, 3) cost threshold, 4) operational ownership. if you need KMS and VPC peering + audit logs then Dedicated or Private typically wins; Hosted is good for fastest time-to-value and cheapest for small scale.
[02:25] Lisa Caldwell: yeah that matches expectations. we'd like a recommended path: do a Hosted functional eval first then run Dedicated/Private benchmarks? or start Dedicated given PHI?
[02:33] Ethan Park: common pattern — run a small Hosted sandbox that uses synthetic/anonymized data to validate model correctness and integration (two weeks), then move to Dedicated for performance and security validation. Private is recommended when you need full on-prem or air-gapped control; given your KMS requirement and VPC residency we should evaluate Dedicated with customer KMS and VPC peering; Private only if Dedicated can't meet audit requirements.
[02:55] Jasmine Lee: can Dedicated support customer-managed keys?
[02:58] Ethan Park: yes, Dedicated supports BYOK with our KMS integration and we can do HSM-backed keys depending on contract. audit logs and retention windows are configurable; we'll send the exact SOC 2 artifacts.
[03:09] Dr. Amir Patel: how about throughput? you said Dedicated gives predictable throughput — what's the sizing model?
[03:14] Ethan Park: we size based on qps, model type, and avg seq length. for your short prompts we estimate a single A100-class slice can handle ~120-160 concurrent short requests depending on batching. for 200 concurrent we'll likely need 2-3 slices with autoscale/burst headroom. exact numbers come from running your traces through our benchmark harness.
[03:33] Lisa Caldwell: batching concerns — we can't increase latency beyond p95 target even if batching saves cost.
[03:38] Ethan Park: totally — our runtime supports latency SLOs with burst policies; we can hold batch sizes small for tail-sensitive endpoints and apply batching to background/long-running jobs. we can also do prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce per-token cost.
[03:52] Nina Gomez: about function calling and structured output — we need high fidelity on coding outputs for billing codes. any eval for deterministic outputs?
[03:59] Ethan Park: we'll include quality evals in the benchmark: prompt sets, golden labels and regression alerts. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles while monitoring quality regressions. we'll share the eval harness and an example spreadsheet.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: timeline wise — if we get the artifacts (anonymized traces, sample prompts, test golden labels) by Feb 7th, Ethan can run initial hosted tests in 1 week, then run dedicated benchmark across two cluster sizes over the following week. so roughly 4-6 weeks to a complete POC report.
[04:28] Ryan Cho: for data movement — do you need us to upload to S3 or can we keep in our VPC and run the benchmark from Private?
[04:33] Ethan Park: we support both. for Hosted tests we ask for sample payloads on secure share (S3 presigned or secure vault). for Dedicated we can do VPC peering and run the benchmark within your VPC, no data egress needed. Private runs fully inside your env.
[04:46] Jasmine Lee: audit trails — retention windows? is there an option to purge raw transcripts?
[04:50] Ethan Park: yes retention and deletion are configurable; we can set shorter retention for POC and show deletion workflows. we'll provide the compliance docs.
[04:58] Lisa Caldwell: cost — can you ballpark Dedicated vs Hosted for our expected load?
[05:02] Sofia Martinez: rough order: hosted cheapest for low steady usage; Dedicated has fixed monthly slice costs but gives predictable per-req cost and performance; Private has highest upfront integration but lowest long-term marginal if you run very large volume. we'll put an example TCO in the SOW with sample numbers.
[05:17] Dr. Amir Patel: what about fallback and graceful degradation? if Dedicated capacity spikes do you offer fallback to hosted?
[05:22] Ethan Park: yes we have smart routing and fallback policies — can route to Hosted as overflow, or to smaller/cheaper model variants with automatic quality gates. we can configure fallback windows and canary rules.
[05:33] Nina Gomez: for benchmarks please include these metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens, quality f1 for coding, and error/retry rates.
[05:43] Ethan Park: noted. we'll include an artifact: a spreadsheet + grafana dashboards and a runbook for reproduceability. we'll provide the harness repo link.
[05:52] Sofia Martinez: any blockers for starting? Jasmine?
[05:55] Jasmine Lee: we need the SOC2 scope and details, plus a support level that includes calendarized incident response for PHI incidents.
[06:03] Sofia Martinez: understood — Maya will attach SOC2 and security pack in the SOW.
[06:07] Maya Rivera: i'll add our pen-testing summary and the SOC2 cover letter.
[06:10] Lisa Caldwell: ok next steps recap?
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: i'll share SOW + pricing by Feb 3. ethan will share benchmark harness by Feb 5. oakridge will send anonymized traces and golden labels by Feb 7. follow-up workshop to be scheduled two weeks after that.
[06:24] Dr. Amir Patel: sounds good, thanks.
[06:26] Sofia Martinez: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the repo and docs.
[06:30] [call ends]
notes: References mentioned: benchmark harness repo (link to be provided), SOC2 package (PDF), SOW template (Google Doc)
Team leaning: Hosted for quick integration tests, Dedicated for security/performance validation, Private if Dedicated can't meet KMS/VPC needs
